output.headline: Sponsor with three prior dental deals and the most Southeast deals on the priority list; fits the $80M target, but returns at the ask are tight.
output.differentiator: Most Southeast deals on the priority list (4, against 3 at the next most active). Its median paid of 15.5x is above Heartland Dental, Aspen Dental and Dental365, though below the largest sponsors.
output.why_them: Repeat dental investor, Southeast-active, pays 15.5x median

acquirer_overview.title: Global sponsor: 18 deals since 2016, 83% closed
points: Financial sponsor with 18 deals from 2016 to 2024; 15 of 18 (83%) closed and 17 of 18 (94%) were control deals [T:record, K:closed_share, K:control_share].
Median deal is $124M, and 8 of 18 deals sit in the $40M-$160M comparable size band. 10 deals were outside provider services [T:record, K:size_band].
Flagship fund of about $25 billion (2022 vintage); approximately $100 billion AUM as of November 2025 [P:1, P:2].

strategic_fit_thesis.title: Prior dental platform investor, already active in the Southeast
points: 3 deals in the target's own sub-sector and 5 in adjacent provider sub-sectors; sector relevance is only a slight factor in its likelihood [T:record, S:sector_rel].
Margin Improvement was a motive in 7 of 18 deals, which suits a target with an 18.0% margin [M:margin_improvement, X:target].
4 deals in the Southeast, the target's region; an $80M deal is not smaller than its usual range, a slight factor [T:record, S:not_smaller].

precedent_activity.title: Two dental platform entries, one of them in the Southeast
points: Metro Dental Care: $46M Platform Investment, Southeast, 2018, at 15.1x. Global Dental Care: $14M Platform Investment, 2016, at 17.0x [D:MA-2018-0091, D:MA-2016-0302].
Summit DSO: $303M Merger of Equals, 2018, at 11.7x. All three dental deals closed [D:MA-2018-0184].
Recent provider deals: Crest Care Partners ($304M, 2024, Southeast, 9.3x) and Crown Addiction Treatment ($123M, 2023, 14.6x) [D:MA-2024-0120, D:MA-2023-0108].

valuation_context.title: 75th percentile is defensible; its 15.5x median supports it
points: 63 comparable deals, 12 in the same sub-sector: 11.0x at the 25th percentile, 13.7x median, 15.4x at the 75th percentile [V:comps].
The 18.0% margin is above the comps' median of 12.4%, supporting upper-quartile pricing. Advent's own median paid is 15.5x [V:comps].
At 5.0x leverage and 8.5% interest, equity cheque is $53M. IRR at the ask is 14.0% against a 20% target; maximum price is $68M [V:lbo].

risk_flags.title: Return at the asking price
risk_flags.concern: IRR at the ask of 14.0% is below its 20% target [V:lbo].
risk_flags.mitigant: Its own median paid of 15.5x shows it pays upper-quartile multiples [V:comps].
risk_flags.reality: Maximum price is $68M on both exit cases, against an $80M EV, so a platform exit does not close the gap [V:lbo, X:target].

risk_flags.title: No open dental platform
risk_flags.concern: Advent has no open platform in the sub-sector, so the target would not be a clear add-on [A:angles].
risk_flags.mitigant: It made two Platform Investments in dental, in 2016 and 2018 [D:MA-2016-0302, D:MA-2018-0091].
risk_flags.reality: Its dental deals are all from 2016 and 2018; the target would need a new platform thesis [T:record, A:angles].

risk_flags.title: Crowded process, low rank
risk_flags.concern: It is 10th on the priority list with a likelihood of 4.5%, and auction experience is a slight factor against [R:rank, S:bidder_exp].
risk_flags.mitigant: Control deals are 17 of 18 and 15 of 18 closed [K:control_share, K:closed_share].
risk_flags.reality: Heartland Dental and Aspen Dental have each closed every deal and have a dental-only record, so Advent must win on price.

conviction.rationale: Three own-sub-sector and five adjacent provider deals support the fit. Medium because there is no open platform in the sub-sector and the return at the ask is 14.0% against 20%. [C:conviction, V:lbo]
